question.problem:
The population growth of a developing rural area was studied for $25$ years. The following table shows the population $p(t),$ in hundreds, recorded $t$ years after $1990.$

| **$t$** | $0$ | $5$ | $10$ | $15$ | $20$ | $25$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $p(t)$ | $90$ | $98$ | $116$ | $138$ | $178$ | $220$ |

$$

$$

Approximate the population growth rate in the year $2005$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=5.$
question.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{p}^{′}(x)≈\frac{p(t+h)-p(t-h)}{2h}.
$$

 
We note that year $2005$ corresponds to $t=15.$ The step size is $h=5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(15) & ≈\frac{p(15+5)-p(15-5)}{2(5)} \\  & =\frac{p(20)-p(10)}{2(5)} \\  & =\frac{178-116}{10} \\  & =\frac{62}{10} \\  & =6.2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the population growth rate in $2005$ was $620$ people per year.
